chronoseries.name: Asterias
chronoseries.note: Single extant point. No predecessor chronospecies is assigned. Adjacent scales, not fossil species, are the comparison: cellular tier ~10 µm versus this 115.2 µm wavelength versus an arm-tip organ tier ~1 mm.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg 1979: du/dt = Du lap u + a - u + u^2 v; dv/dt = Dv lap v + b - u^2 v
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (Dv f_u + Du g_v) / (2 Du Dv)

parameters.note: Ratio 7.62 is just above the Schnakenberg onset root (~7.487) so that, on this patch, the p=5 mode (115.2 µm) is unstable and the p=4 mode (144 µm) is not. Not the slot-154 template (alpha=1.23, beta=0.25).

empirical_claims: Turing (1952) gives the diffusion-driven instability and a critical wavenumber. Murray (1981) writes the pre-pattern wavenumber used here.
Schnakenberg (1979) supplies the two-species reaction. The rate constants are chosen for this scale; they were not measured in Asterias epidermis.

Garm & Nilsson (2014) show that starfish carry a compound eye at the arm tip. Their behavioural subject is Linckia laevigata. The abstract's anatomical statement is transferred to Asteroidea, including Asterias, and is not a 115.2 µm measurement.
Pass-1 2D radial FFT wavelength on the square patch was 116.4904 µm against the catalog 115.2 µm (Pearson r of analytical vs FTCS sigma(k) = 0.999817, RMSE = 0.003533 per tau, KS = 0.0833).

specimen.note: Organism-scale studio photograph from the Belgian continental shelf. It has no scale bar. It is not a 115.2 µm micrograph. The project gallery plate datasets/species_gallery/II_Anaima_Invertebrata/Asterias_rubens.jpg was the instructed fallback and was not used, because this CC-licensed photograph was retrieved.

pass2_measurements.note: Spacing reference is the within-plate 10th percentile. The silhouette/square std ratio is the R1 negative control. The photograph has no scale bar.
